title: Embedding vector dimensionality migration and reindex guidance
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: We need a safe, low-latency path to change the canonical dimensionality of embeddings produced by Redwood's embeddings endpoint and the reranking pipeline. This ticket centralizes the migration strategy, client guidance, and reindexing playbook for customers and internal vector stores. Goals: 1) Minimize client breakage and downtime during dim changes, 2) Keep query latency and memory cost under SLO targets during transition, 3) Provide clear guidance and automation for reindexing and aliasing, 4) Ensure metrics and rollback hooks are available.
motivation: Embedding model improvements and quantization updates will change vector length for several curated models. Some customers rely on fixed-dim downstream stores and similarity pipelines; without a migration plan this can cause failed writes, incorrect similarity scoring, or silent quality regressions in reranking. We must support both internal vector index migration and provide documented client-side strategies.
migration_plan: 1) Support multi-dim compatibility in the embeddings API: return metadata.dimensions with each embedding and accept an explicit ?expected_dim= query param for strict-mode clients.

2) Introduce index aliasing in vector-store service: new index created with v2-dim, existing index kept as read-only for fallback; alias points to primary index for queries and can be flipped atomically.
3) Reindex strategy: bulk reindex snapshot -> incremental replay -> cutover. Use a short dual-write window to avoid lost updates (write to both indices and track seq numbers).

4) Projection helpers: provide server-side projection functions for temporary compatibility: zero-padding, truncation, and learned linear projection (small adapter matrix) for best-quality backfill when full reindex isn't immediately possible.

5) Rollout: staged rollout by customer tier and region. Start with internal canary, then low-risk customers, then broader audience. Feature-flag the strict-mode to force reject mismatched dims for high-confidence clients.
6) Telemetry and safety nets: emit dim-mismatch metrics, reindex progress dashboards, and automatic rollback if query quality drops beyond threshold defined in quality tests.
7) Documentation and client guidelines: examples for FAISS/Milvus/Pinecone, sample reindex scripts, and recommended client-side validation code.
8) Deadline: complete core automation and internal reindex for top-5 affected models by 2026-04-01 per release plan.
acceptance_criteria: API augments embedding response with metadata.dimensions and accepts expected_dim param (tests included)
Vector-store supports index aliasing and atomic alias flip in console and API
Reindex path documented and validated end-to-end with a customer-like dataset (<= 1M vectors) without violating latency SLOs
Projection helpers available in SDK and validated with quality regression tests showing acceptable drop (<= 3% NDCG@10 for reranking baseline) when projection used
Monitoring dashboards show dim-mismatch counts, reindex progress, and query latency under 95th percentile SLO during migration
Client-facing migration guide published and reviewed by PM and Developer Experience
risks: Quality degradation if naive projection (zero-pad/truncate) used long-term
Index storage costs double during dual-index period, leading to unexpected billing spikes
Customer code that assumes fixed dim may break client-side validation, causing failed ingestion
On-the-fly projection at query time can add CPU overhead and increase tail latency
Edge-case models that change both dim and embedding distribution may not be recoverable without full re-encode
client_communication: Pre-announcement email to affected customers 2 weeks before cutover with explicit dates and tooling links
Migration guide with step-by-step instructions: detect dim changes, run bulk backfill, enable dual-write, flip alias, retire old index
Code snippets for client SDKs: how to validate dimensions, how to call embeddings with expected_dim, and reprojection examples
Template support ticket text for customers who cannot reindex immediately (we offer server-side adapter for 90 days)
FAQ: billing impact, expected downtime (none), quality trade-offs for temporary projection
implementation_notes: API: embed responses now include 'meta.dimensions' string field and we add optional 'expected_dim' query param. Default behavior remains backward compatible.
SDKs: add dimension metadata parsers and helper reproject functions in python/js sdks
Vector-store: add aliasing layer to index manager; implement atomic alias swap using metadata-backed compare-and-swap
Backfill tooling: use snapshot export from primary storage, run batch encoder on GPU pool, stream into new index with checkpointing
Dual-write: data-plane shim to write to both indices; idempotency via write-token and sequence numbers
Quality tests: run evals on representative prompt sets for reranking and semantic search; track NDCG and MRR changes
Infra: estimate temporary storage increase and request quota bump for top-10 customers during backfill
tests: Unit tests for API metadata and expected_dim validation
Integration test: write to dual indices and read from alias with correctness checks
Load test: reindex 1M vectors while serving queries; measure 95th percentile latency
Quality regression harness: run reranking evaluation suite pre- and post-projection
Chaos test: simulate partial reindex and ensure fallback to old index without data loss
rollback_plan: If rerank quality drops > 5% or latency SLO violated, flip alias back to old index and pause new-index writes
Stop dual-write and reschedule backfill with increased resources if necessary
Notify customers and provide timeline for corrective action
Tag the problematic model release and revert model-version mapping in model-catalog if root cause is model change
